fullPassage: Dry heat is often less dangerous than wet heat — the more humid the air is, the more difficult it is for our sweat to evaporate and dissipate heat. And like all living things, our bodies have thermal limits. Those limits vary depending on age, general health, and a number of other factors. But most researchers agree that a wet bulb temperature of 95 degrees, basically meaning both outdoor air temperature and humidity levels are high, is the upper end of human adaptability to humid heat. Humid heat has been associated with increased demand for more accurate sensors to measure environmental temperatures. Beyond that, our body generates heat faster than it can dissipate it.
